clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s constellation of obesity, stage 1 hypertension, and prediabetic HbA1c fulfills criteria for metabolic syndrome, which is the most probable unifying diagnosis. Essential hypertension is also clearly present. A normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis suggests proximal renal tubular acidosis, though urine studies are lacking. Prediabetes is confirmed by HbA1c and carries a moderate risk of progression. Obstructive sleep apnea remains a remote possibility given obesity but lacks supporting symptomatology.
unresolved_findings: Normal‑anion‑gap metabolic acidosis – etiology not yet identified (proximal RTA vs chronic gastrointestinal bicarbonate loss)
Low‑normal random glucose (66.7 mg/dL) – fasting status unknown
Missing fasting lipid panel (total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides)
Missing eGFR and urine albumin‑creatinine ratio to assess renal function
No documented sleep‑related symptoms to confirm OSA
Serum vitamin B12 level not available (potential deficiency)
Smoking and alcohol use not captured
recommended_workup: Serum creatinine, eGFR, and urine albumin‑creatinine ratio
Urine electrolytes, urine pH, urine anion gap, and urine ammonium to characterize RTA
Comprehensive medication review for agents causing bicarbonate loss
Polysomnography or home sleep apnea testing
Repeat fasting glucose and HbA1c in 3–6 months
